To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the implementation and development, on a large-scale, of a new model for the organization of the health services in the city of RIo de Janeiro, Brazil, was possible only due to a political decision that gave priority to the development of primary care, in the period 2009 to the 2016, and that this political decision was not maintained by the municipal government in the following term (2017 2018).
The adoption of OSS in the city of RJ was a strategy to expand and improve PHC coverage, but its sustainability was not ensured.
the implementation and development, as well as the dismantling of PPPs for PHC, in the city of RJ, were associated with the political choice of the municipal government.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the need to understand the political and institutional context that makes possible or not the adoption of certain models of management and organization of health services.

the need to understand the dynamics of PHC development in the city of RJ, which has been marked by a strong oscillation between the outsourcing of the management and the return of the management to the municipality.

the need to deepen the understanding of the factors that contribute to the expansion and improvement of the PHC in Rio de Janeiro, and to understand the challenges and opportunities that arise from the implementation of the OSS model in the management of PHC.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the adoption and sustainability of the OSS model in the PHC management in the city was directly associated with the municipal government's political decision and not with the municipality's economic conditions.

, in the case of Rio de Janeiro's PHC, the adoption of the PPP model was associated with the improvement of PHC indicators and the expansion of the service network, as well as the development of the OSS model, and that this model was vetoed by the new government, which, despite the economic difficulties, opted for the return to the traditional model of public administration.
, in the city of RJ, the OSS model was not the cause of the expansion and improvement of PHC coverage indicators.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the OSS model, in addition to the organizational and management innovations it brings to the SUS, can also contribute to the expansion of PHC.

, despite the challenges and difficulties, the experience of the city of Rio has shown the importance of adopting the OSS model in the management of PHC in Brazil, as a strategy to overcome the barriers of the SUS and improve the population's access to health services.

the experience of the city of Rio in relation to the adoption of the organizational model of Social Organizations in the management of Primary Care, in a large scale, has shown that this is a viable option for the expansion of PHC and for improving the coverage indicators of the SUS in Brazil.
The main takeaway from our work is that

the OSS model is an important organizational option to expand PHC, but its sustainability depends on the political will of the government in power.
